blurb:
If you're the type to actually use your gear — running the trails around the lake, playing pickup ball, or just spending enough time outside that your shoes take a beating — the Nike Clearance Store at Grapevine Mills is worth knowing about.

It's a clearance outlet, so the selection rotates and you won't always find every size, but reviewers have spotted shoes marked down to $15 and apparel priced well below what you'd find in a standard retail Nike store. The tradeoff is that the inventory isn't guaranteed — you're hunting a little, which some people love and some people find annoying.

The reviews are mixed enough to be honest. Most shoppers walk out happy with what they found. A few have run into pricing confusion at checkout, so worth paying attention when something looks too good to be true.

For active families around the lake who go through athletic shoes at a steady clip, it's a reasonable stop when you're already making the drive toward Grapevine. Clearance store prices on a brand that holds up well outdoors is a combination that's hard to argue with when the sizes line up.
hours: Mon–Thu 10:00 AM – 8:00 PM, Fri–Sat 10:00 AM – 9:00 PM, Sun 11:00 AM – 7:00 PM
address: 3000 Grapevine Mills Pkwy Ste 611, Grapevine, TX 76051, USA
scoring_notes: National chain clearance outlet outside the search areas with mixed reviews and limited community connection; weakest fit of the three candidates.

blurb:
Sometimes the best shopping trip is the one where you had no real plan going in. T.J. Maxx and HomeGoods sharing the same roof is exactly that kind of place — you walk in for one thing and leave with three others you didn't know you needed.

The Irving location on MacArthur pulls solid reviews for being well-stocked and not overcrowded, which matters more than people admit. One shopper described falling hard for a dress she never would have tried on somewhere else. Another called out cashier Delilah by name for having the kind of warm, genuinely bubbly energy that actually makes the checkout line feel like a good part of the trip rather than the end of it.

On the HomeGoods side, you're looking at kitchenware, décor, outdoor furniture, and the kind of random finds that end up being the thing guests ask about for years. For lake house decorating on a budget, or just refreshing a space without paying full retail, this combo store covers a lot of ground.

It sits outside the immediate lake communities but is close enough to fold into a shopping run when you're heading toward the city.
address: 7735 N MacArthur Blvd, Irving, TX 75063, USA
scoring_notes: National chain located outside the search areas with no meaningful connection to the Lewisville Lake community specifically.

blurb:
If you spend any real time out on Lewisville Lake, you already know the feeling of realizing mid-trip that you forgot something. Wrong weight line. Not enough hooks. Nobody brought sunscreen. Bass Pro in Grapevine is the fix for all of that, and then some.

This location gets called out specifically by reviewers for being clean, well-organized, and easier to navigate than most stores its size. And the staff in the fishing section draws real praise — the kind of specific, enthusiastic compliments that usually only happen when someone actually knows what they're talking about and genuinely wants to help you catch something.

Beyond fishing gear, they stock hunting equipment, camping supplies, apparel, and enough lake-ready gear to outfit a full weekend party. The store has a wilderness-themed layout that makes the whole thing feel like more than a shopping run — families with kids tend to treat it as a destination on its own. At a 4.5 rating across over 6,300 reviews, it has earned that reputation.

It's about 25 minutes south on 121, worth building into a pre-trip supply run.
hours: Mon–Sat 9:00 AM – 9:00 PM, Sun 10:00 AM – 7:00 PM
address: 2501 Bass Pro Dr, Grapevine, TX 76051, USA
scoring_notes: Strong relevance to Lewisville Lake's outdoor/fishing audience and high review volume, but it is a national chain outside the core search areas.
